No existing QA axis (voice / wall / q-usage / canonical / detangler / bib / proof / compute) measures clarity of the statement itself. Use when asked to "bold defined terms", "tighten definitions", "no rambling definitions", "one definition per block", "tight theorem/proposition/lemma statements", or to set up / run a clarity audit. Also runs the inverse audit — a non-`definition` block that secretly carries a definition (`clarity-defn-misplaced`) — plus a statement-purity check (`clarity-stmt-pure`: a theorem/prop/lemma/conjecture carries only its claim; embedded remark / interpretation moves to a follow-on `remark`) and a register check (`clarity-grad-style`: graduate-level formal-math prose — no contractions, second-person, hype, colloquialism, or emoji). Emits per-block QA sidecar params under the `clarity-*` criteria via `folio/pipeline/definition-clarity-audit.ts`.

Each swarm agent owns its own branch (commits, pushes, opens a PR); the foreground session runs auto prepare-merge on each swarm branch and repeats batch-by-batch until the paper is completely drained. Sister to `/integration-backlog` (that drains watcher findings; this drains exposition quality).

@graph.name: latex-build-cache

@graph.name: compute-QA: are the computations and witnesses sound?
@graph.summary: Run qou's compute-QA gates over `computations/` and its witnesses, and publish one verdict per gate to the `qa-reports` branch.
@graph.description:
Run qou's compute-QA gates over `computations/` and its witnesses, and publish one verdict per gate to the `qa-reports` branch.

WHY ONE PROCESS. The gates used to live as inline steps in four workflow files, so nothing named them as a set, and the order an agent ran them in locally was whatever it remembered. They are now one table (`scripts/compute-qa.py`) and this one diagram; the workflows call the table, and each step carries a `# bpmn-node:` back-reference here.

THE COMMANDS DID NOT CHANGE. Each gate runs the exact command the workflow step ran, with the same exit-code handling: a strict gate fails on a non-zero exit, a warn or advisory gate never fails the run and its output is the report; when it exits non-zero its verdict is WARN rather than PASS, so a finding is not recorded as green. Measured on `main` before the move and after it, every gate's exit codes and output are identical.

QA IS AGENT-OWNED; CI IS A BACKUP. These workflows are dispatch-only (owner directive 2026-06-30, Actions billing), and several have never run. So the normal way through this process is an agent running `python3 scripts/compute-qa.py` before it commits, not CI. The lane says who runs a gate, not where.

THREE OUTCOMES. A gate whose script cannot start (a missing module or binary) is UNKNOWN and never a pass. A failing self-test fails its gate whatever the gate's mode, because a detector that has stopped matching its known positive reports everything clean.

VERDICTS ARE NOT COMMITTED. Each gate writes `test/results/compute-qa/<gate>.json`, which is gitignored and is the layout `bun run qa:publish` reads.

A gate failed: fix at the producer, never widen a baseline

Is the generated Lean in sync with its generators?
@graph.summary: Check that the Lean text a script in this repository writes is still exactly what that script writes.
@graph.description:
Check that the Lean text a script in this repository writes is still exactly what that script writes. Two files carry such text: every knot block of `QOU/Knot/GeneratedGluing.lean` (from `scripts/gen-gluing-lean.py`) and the depth-3 corner column `BokutShiaoCornerDepth3` in `UGB/GrobnerShirshov/HeckeCompletion.lean` (from `scripts/gen-hecke-corner-column.py 3`).

WHY IT IS STRICT. These are proofs. If a generator and its output part company, a Lean file that compiles is carrying certificates nothing in the repository produces, and the next regeneration silently changes a proof. The check is cheap (about nine seconds) and writes nothing, so strictness costs nothing.

THREE OUTCOMES, NOT TWO. A generator that cannot run, most often because SnapPy is not installed, is UNKNOWN and never reported as in sync. That is the parity rule the witness-parity Tool already follows.

WHAT IS NOT CHECKED, AND WHY. The depth-2 column `BokutShiaoCorner` (section 4ad) was written by hand first; the generator was checked against it by re-deriving the same words and rules, not the same text. Measured 2026-10-05, the two differ on 964 lines while proving the same thing, so a textual diff there would report drift that is not drift. The module header of GeneratedGluing.lean and its closing `end` line are hand-written too, and are excluded from the comparison for the same reason.

DRIFT IS A DECISION, NOT A FIX. When the regenerated text differs, either the generator changed (and the Lean should be regenerated) or the Lean was edited by hand (and the generator should learn the edit, or the edit should go). Which one is right is a judgement about a proof, so it goes to the author; the agent does not overwrite either side.

@graph.name: A generator or a generated Lean file changed
Unknown: a generator could not run (not a pass)
Decide: regenerate the Lean, or fix the generator?
Refresh computation witnesses
@graph.summary: Bring qou's computation witnesses back in line with the producers that write them, without a witness ever being rewritten that the owner did not approve.
@graph.description:
Bring qou's computation witnesses back in line with the producers that write them, without a witness ever being rewritten that the owner did not approve. Owner, 2026-10-04: "all witnesses tools will need to go into the KG"; this is the process those Tools run in.

A WITNESS IS CONTENT HERE. Its numbers are what the paper quotes, so the owner's rule that a migration changes no mathematics applies to it, and so does the ask-first rule for refreshing one. That is why the decision sits in the owner's lane between the measurement and the re-run, and why nothing before it writes a file: the dry run and the parity check both work on the committed tree or a scratch copy of it.

THE PLAN IS `run_pipeline.py --dry-run --content-only`, UNCHANGED. The process does not re-derive staleness; it calls the pipeline's own answer through the `witness-refresh-plan` Tool, so the list a person approves is exactly the list the pipeline would act on.

@graph.name: folio
@graph.description: The authored folios: quantum-observable-universe and its siblings, each a directory holding a same-named manifest. NOT `folio/` — see `_comment`.

@graph.name: library
@graph.description: L1 source content: one directory per ingested document, and reference DATASETS (e.g. CODATA) whose values are addressable as {{ qou.library.<entry>.<slug> }}.

@graph.name: references
@graph.description: The bibliography: one CSL-JSON entry per file, `<key>.json`, each a `folio-reference/v1` Reference node; folio/schema/references.ts loads them in its ORDER list and references.bib is generated from them (bean qou-l7pj).

@graph.name: computations
@graph.description: Python computations and the witnesses they write (<name>.witness.json). A witness value is addressable in prose as {{ qou.computations.<witness>.<json path> }}, resolved once for the PDF, the blueprint and the site.

@graph.name: tools
@graph.description: qou's Tool nodes: one per computation script a content block wires to a witness, generated from the block manifests by scripts/gen-producer-tools.ts (story TOOLS T5, bean qou-a3l1).

@graph.name: processes
@graph.description: qou's BPMN processes, grouped by concern (processes/processes.json). First: content/witness-refresh.bpmn, the owner-gated refresh of computation witnesses (story TOOLS T6, bean qou-kumy).

@graph.name: qa
@graph.description: What a QA process produced about this folio, published to the qa-reports branch keyed by commit and never committed (owner ruling 2026-10-04, decision 11: QA results go to the cat-harness qa-reports store). It holds what the writers declared under `qa.writers` produce (owner decision 2026-11-24, the integrated QA page): the compute-QA verdicts, one qou-compute-qa/v1 file per gate under compute-qa/ (scripts/compute-qa.py, TOOLS T7, bean qou-4dj1), the Lean vacuity/axiom audit under lean/, and the rendered-paper record under rendering/. Published by .github/workflows/compute-qa.yml (a caller of the platform's layer-qa-publish.yml) and, after a merge, by scripts/qa-publish-local.sh. The directory is gitignored except for a .gitkeep, so it is present in every checkout and a reader never mistakes an absent directory for a clean run. Story S3, bean qou-4rhu.

@graph.name: attestations
@graph.description: The JUDGEMENT half of QA, kept on main where a git rm of derived results cannot reach it (platform kind `attestations`, schema qa-attestations/v1). Holds the two bibliography judgement ledgers since 2026-10-05 (C9 stories B3/B4): `bib-verification/` (the source ledger, formerly folio/bib-qa-verifications.json, 456 rows in one file per reference) and `bib-human-review/` (formerly folio/schema/references.review.json). Read and written only through the platform's cat-harness/schemas/bib-attestations.ts; Python readers use scripts/lib/bib_ledger.py.

@graph.name: lake-cache

contentSource.keyFrom: <package>-<toolchain-slug>, or toolchain-<slug>, or an addon suffix such as qou-v4-24-0-mathlib-gap-modules

@graph.description: Lean build caches, one orphan branch per package and toolchain, restored so a build starts warm. Declared here, on the folio that builds the Lean packages, rather than as a row in folio-assistant's special-branches.json (owner, 2026-10-03). MIGRATED 2026-10-05 (owner: "migratez qou") from the legacy `lake-cache/<member>` names: scripts/lib/lake-cache-family.sh writes the declared name and reads it first, falling back to `lake-cache/<member>`, whose branches are kept and never deleted (AGENTS.md rule 9). `lake-cache/` is where a member is mounted; the restore scripts untar into `.lake/`, which the dot-prefix guard forbids declaring.

@graph.name: wheel-cache
@graph.description: Built wheels of qou's native Python extensions, today only `pyhecke-native` (not on PyPI; a maturin build takes about 2.5 min per container). One orphan branch per package, version, CPython tag, platform and source key, where the source key hashes the git trees of `tools/pyhecke-native` and `tools/hecke-engine`. Read and written by scripts/wheel-cache.sh, which keeps its git objects in a private bare repository rather than the checkout; scripts/build-pyhecke-native.sh restores before it builds by default, but seeds origin only when PYHECKE_NATIVE_PUSH=1 (and never when PYHECKE_NATIVE_NO_SEED=1), after a clean build passes its convention gate. `wheel-cache/` is where a member is mounted; nothing is tracked there. Bean qou-dgkf.

@graph.name: qou-typologies
@graph.description: The graph typologies qou owns, one folio-graph-typology/v1 node per file. There is no central registry for subgraph types (owner, 2026-10-04): a harness declares its own. Today it holds `wheel-cache`, the kind of the directory above.

@graph.name: trace-cache

contentSource.keyFrom: <function>-<engine-key>-q<q-key>-dps<dps>, e.g. tr-m-atomic-mpfr-suffixes-<12 hex>-q<12 hex>-dps40; function is tr-m-atomic-mpfr or tr-m-atomic-mpfr-suffixes, one member per route because two routes to one exact value may round its last digits differently; engine-key hashes the git trees of tools/hecke-engine and tools/pyhecke-native (the wheel-cache source key), q-key hashes the q0 decimal string

@graph.description: Exact results of qou's native trace producers (`pyhecke_native.tr_m_atomic_mpfr` and `tr_m_atomic_mpfr_suffixes`), stored so a long probe run resumes and a re-run recomputes nothing. One orphan branch per producer function, engine source key, q0 string and dps; inside it, content-addressed JSONL shards of (n, signed word, suffix) -> the producer's exact decimal string, never a float. A dirty engine tree has no key, so a stale value is never served, and `computations/trace_cache.py` re-evaluates a sample of loaded entries against the live binary before using any. Read and written by scripts/trace-cache.sh, whose git objects live in a private bare repository; computations/trace_cache.py restores by default but seeds origin only when QOU_TRACE_CACHE_PUSH=1; a seed adds a shard on top of the tip and never forces. `trace-cache/` is where a member is mounted; nothing is tracked there. The kind is `typologies/trace-cache.json`.

@graph.name: mn-chi-cache

contentSource.keyFrom: mn-chi-q-<engine-key>, where engine-key is the wheel-cache / trace-cache source key (git trees of tools/pyhecke-native and tools/hecke-engine)

@graph.description: Exact values of `pyhecke_native.mn_chi_q(lambda, mu)`, the q-Murnaghan-Nakayama Hecke character table, stored so a sweep that needs a heavy table (n = 24, 27) computes each entry once. One orphan branch per engine source key; inside it, content-addressed JSONL shards of (lambda, mu) -> the producer's exact [q-degree, coefficient-string] pairs, never a float. Before 2026-11-22 this was the in-tree file computations/.derived-chi-mn-cache.json, keyed by (lambda, mu) alone, so an entry from one engine build was served to every later one. Read and written by computations/derived_chi_catalogue_mn_disk_cache.py through the shared layer (scripts/lib/branch-cache.sh, computations/_branch_cache.py); it restores by default but seeds origin only when QOU_MN_CHI_CACHE_PUSH=1.
